From the finite catalogue to every finite packing

This is a human metatheorem supported by exact computation and independent review, rather than a proof-assistant derivation. For any finite set of distinct placements of this prototype under the declared group and integer translations, the original angular field satisfies

\[ \forall p\in\mathbb Z^2,\quad \sum_{Q\in\mathcal P}t_Q(p)\le1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall Q\ne R\in\mathcal P,\quad\operatorname{int}Q\cap\operatorname{int}R=\varnothing. \]

In the forward direction, nonnegative weights make every pair capacity-legal. Normalize either tile to the root using the verified lattice group; the complete catalogue, together with separated bounding boxes outside its envelope, then excludes polygon overlap.

In the reverse direction, each angular weight counts the occupied local sectors of angle \(\pi/6\). Interior-disjoint polygons cannot occupy the same local open sector, so the total is at most twelve sectors at every lattice point. This argument uses actual sector disjointness: pairwise weighted capacity alone would not justify the aggregate inequality.

The independent carrier checker verifies the prototype's sector density, including every zero-valued lattice point in its bounding box; the signed-coordinate group preserves the sector grid. This proves packing faithfulness under the stated assumptions. It does not establish plane coverage or existence of a tiling. Read the complete proof review.

The optional periodic carrier

Positive support counts: \(28\) old angular, \(240\) occupancy, and \(268\) combined. Independent carrier receipt: VERIFIED. All \(12\) cells/samples are displayed. Common integer scale \(S=18\). Primitive normal families: \(\{(0,1),(1,-1),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,1)\}\).

The complete carrier is the union of integer translates of these phases, not every point on the displayed fine grid:

\[ \Lambda=\bigcup_i(q_i+\mathbb Z^2)\subseteq S^{-1}\mathbb Z^2. \]

The selected pair's group determines the displayed saved phase permutation and integer shift. These are certified data, not a browser recomputation.

Why this carrier detects all positive-area overlaps, conditionally

Let the primitive integer normals be \(\mathcal N\), and use every integer line \(n\cdot x=k\). Every allowed polygon edge must lie on one of those lines. The coordinate-grid normals and their full group orbit are included, so clipping to the unit square does not create an artificial noninvariant subdivision.

\[ \mathcal A=\{x:n\cdot x=k,\ n\in\mathcal N,\ k\in\mathbb Z\}. \]

Interior membership is constant on every open two-dimensional arrangement cell. A nonempty overlap of two polygon interiors contains an open cell, so its canonical sample is occupied by both tiles. Conversely, a shared occupied sample is itself an interior-overlap witness. Thus binary sample capacity detects pairwise interior overlap for the complete carrier under these hypotheses.

The normal action is contragredient, \(n\mapsto nR^{-1}\). Integer intercept phases are preserved by integer translations and the verified integer group. Each sample is the arithmetic mean of the cell's distinct canonical extreme vertices; affine maps preserve that mean. The saved phase action checks its image as \(Rq_i=q_j+z\). The independent carrier receipt also checks the complete support, cells, angular units and phase compositions.

In the combined field, old angular points retain their exact sector weights and occupied cell samples contribute \(12\), with common capacity \(12\) and no markings. This is a new point representation when it excludes an old legal overlap. It is not a proved redundant constraint in the old sampled model.

Completeness of the relative-pair catalogue and its limits

Verified group closure, inverses and integer unimodularity let one placement be moved to the identity root without changing the allowed relative system. For each second orientation, the inclusive integer ranges are

\[ \min_xP-\max_x(RP)\le d_x\le\max_xP-\min_x(RP), \]\[ \min_yP-\max_y(RP)\le d_y\le\max_yP-\min_y(RP). \]

Outside these ranges the closed axial bounding boxes are separated, hence the polygon interiors are disjoint. The authored supports are bounded by their polygons, so separated boxes also share no occupied support. Inside the envelope, all pairs are included, including contacts sharing no old sample; root-identical placements and equivalent placements are explicitly counted as exclusions/deduplications.

The saved run exhausted this declared catalogue. The carrier argument assumes the stated integer translation lattice and allowed group. New orientations, nonlattice translations or boundary phases need requalification. An arbitrary fixed or movable region boundary may cut cells and needs its own exact boundary authoring.

What this establishes. This qualifies geometry versus point capacity and checks a point-carrier construction. Markings remain empty. It supplies no learned matching rule, RL result, substitution rule, practical region-tiling benchmark, fair untouched-point growth proof or tiling of the plane.

The polygon and literal vertex weights were transcribed from byte-pinned public snapshots of GCTS-I.html and the A2 engine. The local historical files were unavailable as hydrated data and were not opened; equivalence to locally modified files is not claimed. The old scientific JavaScript and its known matching rules were not imported or executed.

The frozen native model uses exact integer/rational arithmetic and empty markings. Capacity is the point-value rule from the shared algorithm contract; polygon tests are independent verification. This study has no search frontier, scheduler or rollback implementation to certify. The existing finite-boundary engine's extra geometric controls and the infinite-growth fair-activation obligation remain separate work.

The protocol and source pins were frozen before scientific execution. It changed neither the catalogue, resource limits nor scientific inputs. The full archive preserves both freezes, raw oracle certificates, independent catalogue audit, source snapshots and execution logs.
